video_title: How to Make it in Crypto (without getting lucky) - Jez
gist: Jez (ex-HFT options market maker, Millennium quant, Standard Crypto VC) argues revenue-generating perp DEX tokens (Hyperliquid, Lighter, Variational) are decoupling from crypto cycles because perps will cannibalize retail options under a 'long degeneracy' macro, values assets by expected marginal flows ('new coin good, old coin bad'), and introduces Paper Trade, a 1000x zero-slippage perps primitive on HyperEVM bootstrapped from trader losses via precompile oracles. He also lays out his risk lessons: high-conviction spot built every comeback while low-conviction leverage punts caused every blowup.

themes.theme: Perps as the secular growth trade

insights.claim: Jez argues that revenue-generating perp exchange tokens that return value to holders have become far less cyclical, so whether the broad crypto market is bull or bear matters little to his positioning.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Fundamental, buyback-backed exchange tokens may be evaluated independently of BTC cycle calls.
insights.quote: I think hype holders haven't really noticed a bull or a bear

insights.claim: Jez's core long-term thesis is that perpetual futures will cannibalize the retail short-dated (including zero-day) options market, a view rooted in his years as an HFT options market maker against 2015-2019 Wall Street Bets-style traders seeking high-delta leverage.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: The addressable market for perp venues is the retail options/leverage-seeking pie, not just existing crypto volume.

insights.claim: Jez says his exit signal for the perps thesis is not a HYPE or LIT price target but when it becomes consensus that options are dying because of perps, e.g. people writing threads on 'the death of options because of perps'.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Defines a narrative-based (not price-based) take-profit trigger for perp-exchange tokens.
insights.quote: When people are writing threads on the death of options because of PERS, then you're like, okay, it's had a real impact on the options market.

insights.claim: Jez believes the whole perps market is still going to 10x, so owning 'the house' (exchange tokens) works almost regardless of individual market share.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Supports a basket approach across perp DEX tokens rather than a single-winner bet.
insights.quote: This whole market I think is still going to 10x.

insights.claim: Jez dismisses the argument that HYPE at roughly $94 is too expensive, saying perp exchanges should be valued as pure growth businesses rather than steady-state ones, so revenue multiples are not the relevant metric.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Valuation pushback on HYPE based on multiples is, in his view, the wrong frame while sector growth continues.

insights.claim: Jez notes that good exchange-type assets have already been decoupled for years: HYPE has decoupled since launch and BNB has essentially never gone through a bear market.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Exchange tokens with cash flows have a track record of cycle independence, undermining four-year-cycle templates.

insights.claim: Jez observes that most of his successful trades historically have been exchanges: Uniswap, GMX, Rollbit, dYdX, Hyperliquid, Lighter and Variational.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Exchange/venue tokens are a repeatable hunting ground for his edge.

insights.claim: Jez says an underlying tailwind belief that the perps market will grow makes it much easier to hold any asset in that class through drawdowns.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Sector-level conviction can substitute for single-asset conviction during volatility.

insights.claim: Jez argues derivatives are net harmful to crypto's capital base, which keeps getting wiped out on -5% moves, but speculation demand is an unstoppable societal force, so the best outcome is funneling people into perps rather than options because he has seen more success stories from perps.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Retail leverage demand is structural; the investable question is which venue captures it.
insights.quote: Like probably like the world would be a better place if everyone just stuck to spot.

themes.theme: Long degeneracy and crypto's product-market fit

insights.claim: Jez defines 'long degeneracy' as the thesis that risk-taking increases when real returns compress, e.g. when the traditional path of college, job, marriage and home ownership stops working in the cities young people want to live in.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Macro driver for persistent retail speculation demand that underpins exchange and casino-like protocols.
insights.quote: essentially what it is is that um risk increases when real returns compress.

insights.claim: Jez says crypto's real product-market fit is as a financial database with programmable money, but onboarding almost always happens through speculation, typically by seeing someone you think you're smarter than make money.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: User acquisition in crypto is driven by FOMO/status comparison, which favors speculative venues.

insights.claim: Jez warns that the slow-and-steady compounder probably outperforms the 20-year-old long-degeneracy speculator on average, even though the statistical outliers among speculators win big.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Long degeneracy is a thesis to position for (own the house), not a personal strategy to emulate.

insights.claim: Jez explicitly distinguishes long degeneracy as a positioning thesis from his own blowups, which he attributes to greed, poor risk management and tilt, such as 10x-ing a large portfolio on ETH to 'make it back'.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Losses came from revenge leverage, not from the macro thesis itself.

themes.theme: Flows-based valuation and market structure this cycle

insights.claim: Jez argues an asset's price outlook depends on expected future marginal flows, not on whether it looks cheap or expensive today, a lesson he took from TradFi: model next week/month/year flows and their delta on price.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Shifts analysis from valuation levels to buyer/seller flow forecasting.
insights.quote: It doesn't matter if it's too expensive if more people are going to buy it.

insights.claim: Jez's 'new coin good, old coin bad' framework holds that new tokens have holders whose theses are not yet complete, while old tokens carry a disillusioned underwater holder base that sells into any recovery and lacks a natural source of new buyers.
insights.speaker: Jez
entities: new coin good old coin bad
insights.so_what: Favors fresh launches with real fundamentals over legacy tokens with overhang.
insights.quote: And who's the set of new buyers for an old thing, right?

insights.claim: Jez notes exceptions to 'old coin bad': genuinely sustainable old protocols like Sky, which survived governance absenteeism and whose USDS he expects most likely to exist in 10 years.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Some legacy DeFi with durable businesses may be mispriced by the new-coin bias.

insights.claim: Jez says the 2020-2024 signal of selling when something trended on Crypto Twitter (and the 2017 'sell when it's on CNBC' rule) works much less now because institutional buyers outside CT keep bidding assets even when 'everyone owns HYPE'.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Consensus-on-CT is no longer a reliable top signal; external institutional flow changes exit timing.

insights.claim: Jez's preferred exit indicators are consensus-based rather than price-based: regulatory clearance, adoption, and the moment TradFi people start explaining his own theses back to him as if he were a newcomer.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Practical, non-price checklist for timing distribution of conviction positions.

insights.claim: Jez and Taiki characterize this as a 'fundamental researcher's dream cycle' where 'mid-curve' consensus holdings like HYPE keep winning because real businesses exist now, whereas prior cycles punished extrapolating short-term revenue.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Holding quality consensus names may be rewarded more than rotation this cycle.
insights.quote: Yeah. I think, you know, this is a a fundamental researcher sort of dream cycle.

insights.claim: Taiki notes Bitcoin is still in the mid-$80Ks, so it is not a clear bull market, yet holders of HYPE, Zcash and Pump are euphoric, and Trade XYZ tickers have appeared on Bloomberg.
insights.speaker: Taiki Maeda
insights.so_what: Dispersion: fundamental/narrative alts outperforming a flat BTC.

insights.claim: Jez says the general public's lack of appetite for buying anything not named HYPE explains why HYPE trades so high while HyperEVM ecosystem 'betas' stay underpriced: holders refuse to sell HYPE to rotate.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: HyperEVM ecosystem assets may remain structurally discounted; don't assume beta catch-up.

insights.claim: Jez says the best opportunities are in assets mispriced due to investor confusion, because most participants lack independent views and simply follow price.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Edge comes from separating business quality from recent price action.

insights.claim: Jez, an adviser to Lighter, kept buying LIT after it launched around $3 and fell below $1, reasoning that the post-TGE drop reflected pre-TGE excitement rather than the underlying business.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Post-TGE drawdowns on quality launches can be buying opportunities; note his adviser conflict.

insights.claim: Jez cites Lighter's competitive advantages as zero-fee trading for retail and its security model, and calls it the shining example of what can be built on Ethereum for decentralization maxis who lacked good places to express that belief.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Lighter may capture an underserved Ethereum-aligned holder base.

themes.theme: Paper Trade: 1000x perps primitive on HyperEVM

insights.claim: Jez and Blur are launching Paper Trade on October 10 (the one-year anniversary of the 10/10 liquidation event): a fully onchain 1000x zero-slippage perps venue where anyone, including a smart contract or agent, gets an atomic position via a contract call once LP reaches about $5M.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: New composable high-leverage DeFi primitive on Hyperliquid's EVM.

insights.claim: Paper Trade bootstraps its house from zero using the 'Martingale protocol' design Jez and Blur published two years ago: LP is built from aggregate user losses, early winners against an empty house receive accrued debt, and PAPER tokens are emitted only to traders who close at a loss.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Token emissions are tied to the protocol gaining health, avoiding mercenary-LP economics.

insights.claim: Jez says the key unlock was HyperEVM precompiles giving a free, gasless, atomic read of the Hyperliquid BBO every one second, making manipulation require jamming eight figures into the Hyperliquid order book.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Precompile oracles enable onchain derivatives without centralized oracle dependency.
insights.quote: So every 1 second we get a free gasless reliable atomic oracle read on the hyperlquid BBO at that point in time

insights.claim: Jez argues precompiles are the most underutilized primitive in crypto, that all chains should have them, and that Paper Trade may be the first to use them at scale a year after they went public, potentially kickstarting a 'DeFi 3.0' of derivatives experimentation.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Watch HyperEVM for a wave of precompile-based derivative protocols.
insights.quote: I think all chains should have pre-ompiles.

insights.claim: Paper Trade copies Rollbit's asymmetric fee: no notional fee, steep take from winners on tiny moves (1-10 bps) to deter oracle-jitter attacks, flattening so traders keep about 90% of profits once price moves 0.5-1%.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Explains the protocol's edge and why delta-neutral farming still pays the house.

insights.claim: Jez explains that at 1000x leverage any notional fee is untenable: a 5 bps taker fee would equal 50% of collateral, so the venue must instead monetize through the asymmetric fee.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Structural reason high-leverage venues need non-standard fee designs.

insights.claim: Jez concedes the most efficient way to farm PAPER is opening delta-neutral long/short positions and closing the loser before liquidation, but argues farmers still pay the asymmetric fee so the LP gains health with every emission.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Sybil/wash farming is economically priced in rather than prevented.

insights.claim: Jez says only Avantis listened to his years of pitching the Rollbit-style 1000x click-trading model, and it produced huge volume relative to its TVL.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Click-trading high-leverage design has a proven volume/TVL edge.

insights.claim: Jez says AI coding tools (Claude, Codex) made the front end feasible without a team, and he expects a 2-3 year window where anyone with an idea can ship before building becomes so commoditized nobody cares about others' products.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Early-mover window for AI-assisted onchain builders is time-limited.

themes.theme: Risk management, sizing and trader psychology

insights.claim: Jez cites a study finding that on a 1-hour timeframe, even traders who were directionally correct became negative EV beyond about 8x leverage because of stochastic volatility.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Practical leverage cap for directional trades; variance plus liquidation kills correct calls.
insights.quote: Even if you were directionally correct about the asset, like you were long and it was up after 1 hour past 8x leverage, uh, trading became minus EV.

insights.claim: Jez says leverage is dangerous partly because it offers effortless size: he has almost never ended a position with less exposure than he started, always FOMO-ing into more.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Pre-commit position size before opening leveraged trades.

insights.claim: Jez lost about 2% of his portfolio on the 10/10 crash due to hard risk limits, then lost slightly more longing BTC from around $103K in early November, which made him realize he was oversized and take a 36-hour trip to the League of Legends finals to reset.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Size limits and forced trading breaks are concrete tilt controls.

insights.claim: Jez says his big comebacks to seven and eight figures always came from high-conviction spot bags with six-to-nine-month theses, while all his losses came from low-conviction, high-leverage punts.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Concentrated spot conviction is the growth engine; leverage punts are the leak.
insights.quote: my downside has been all isolated to these just like low conviction, high leverage punts.

insights.claim: Jez frames sizing by account stage: concentration to grow a small account, diversification to protect a large one, and at seven-to-eight figures liquidity constraints and diminishing quality-of-life returns argue for a Kelly-criterion approach.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Position sizing should scale with edge and liquidity, not ambition.

insights.claim: Jez's 'save your bullets' test borrowed from poker VPIP: before taking a trade, ask whether you'd be happy if it were your only trade this year.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: A simple filter against marginal spots that bleed accounts.

insights.claim: Jez advises not quitting a job to trade until T-bill yield on the portfolio replaces income, since high-conviction investing needs thesis-development time but little holding time.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Employment acts as an 'APR farm' that protects conviction positions from forced selling.

insights.claim: Jez argues markets beat poker because poker is a linear, capped game against opponents with full relevant information, whereas markets let you play against future buyers who don't know about an asset yet.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Edge in markets compounds from information asymmetry with future buyers.

insights.claim: Jez says he has seen more traders fall off through bad jobs or slow builds that force narrow focus than through a single bad trade.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Opportunity cost of focus is a hidden risk for trader-to-builder transitions.

insights.claim: Jez says the most important thing for an aspiring trader is to find a group chat of sharp people early, because it is a leading indicator that critiques ideas before the market's lagging price signal does; his own move to VC came when an anonymous Discord member nominated him to Standard Crypto.
insights.speaker: Jez
insights.so_what: Peer networks provide pre-trade feedback and deal flow.
